title: Another button simulator. Works on mobile.
author: ekim2077
selftext:
I recently discovered button simulator games and one on demonin was pretty advanced. It was fun while it lasted! Both as a learning experience to understand incremental game logic, and because that specific button simulator didn't work on mobile, I decided to recreate it. I also wanted to add a pet companion to the game that helps with the clicking.

The game currently features two themes: Fantasy and Tech. The gameplay is the same for both; only the text and graphics change.

**Play the game here:** [https://yardimli.github.io/absoluteBS2-reloaded/](https://yardimli.github.io/absoluteBS2-reloaded/)

**GitHub Repository:**[https://github.com/yardimli/absoluteBS2-reloaded](https://github.com/yardimli/absoluteBS2-reloaded)

**Gameplay & Mechanics** I think this game idea is currently more of an incremental concept. In its most basic form, it really is just a bunch of buttons, but eventually, all the buttons could be replaced with graphics and animations. Like a 3D theme park game with ride upgrades!

The gameplay is a bit barebones. There are a few "planet" upgrades that increase the number of rows with buttons, adding more multipliers. There is also a mining feature that opens up to add even more multipliers, along with potions and items that do the same. Any button upgrade will reset all your existing button scores. I actually tried removing the auto-reset on upgrades, but it made the game much less fun.

I also added a pet/bot companion that acts as an auto-clicker. You can upgrade it with money, but with that enabled, the game literally plays itself. Initially, the pet was supposed to be "smart" and evolve with upgrades. While the results weren't bad, I felt it would be more interesting if the player was in control. So, I removed the smart pet feature and added controls to the pet dialog, allowing the player to program the pet's click behavior.



Here is a breakdown of how I put it together:

* **Refactoring:** I started by saving the HTML, CSS, and JS files of the original game it’s based on, then parsed the scripts to grab all the images. Since the original game was written before AI, my first few Codex prompts were focused on moving the game logic into multiple JSON files and refactoring the massive single JavaScript file into smaller, manageable modules.
* **UI & Mobile:** Once that worked, my next step was making the UI responsive so the game would actually work well on mobile. Again codex did a pretty good job, but i needed to edit the css and prompt a few times to get the UI to look better.
* **Assets & Graphics:** I had Codex create the Tech and Fantasy themes. I had to go back and forth a few times to get the graphics right. Codex is smart enough to create sprite sheets instead of individual images to keep the style consistent. However, the sheets weren't very precise; when it broke them down, the images were cut wrong and the sizes were all over the place. I took the sprite sheets into Photoshop, sliced the individual images myself, and resized them so they would look harmonious.
* **Manual Edits:** I occasionally had to edit the code when the AI didn't quite understand me. Most of my manual edits were in the CSS. The AI kept treating the UI like a standard webpage instead of a game interface, adding massive paddings, margins, and unnecessary scrollbars. I also had to prompt it a few times to make the dialogs and font sizes uniform, as it kept producing incredibly inconsistent results.

Overall, I'm really happy with how it turned out.
